title: File Permissions & Ownership 🔐
description: Learn chmod, umask, and how to lock down your scripts and data from unauthorised access.

slides.title: The Permission Triad 👥
slides.content:
## Three Roles, Three Actions

Every file has permissions for:
- **User** (owner)
- **Group**
- **Others** (world)

Actions: **r**ead, **w**rite, e**x**ecute.

View with `ls -l`: `-rwxr-x--- 1 alice staff 4096 May 22 script.sh`

quizData.question: What does the permission `-rwxr-x---` mean?

options.text: Owner can read/write/execute, group can read/execute, others have no access

quizData.explanation: The string breaks down: owner `rwx`, group `r-x`, others `---`.

slides.title: chmod: Changing Permissions ⚙️
slides.content:
## Symbolic & Numeric Modes

- Symbolic: `chmod u+x script.sh` (user adds execute)
- Numeric (octal): `chmod 755 script.sh` (owner rwx, group r‑x, others r‑x)

Common values:
- `600` – owner read/write, no one else (private key)
- `644` – owner rw, group/others r (public files)
- `700` – owner rwx, no one else (private script)
- `750` – owner rwx, group r‑x (shared script)

slides.title: Restrict a Script
slides.content: Make it readable and executable only by you:

quizData.question: The octal permission `600` gives owner ___ and group/others no access.
quizData.explanation: 6 = rw (4+2). No bits for group/others, so they get nothing.

slides.title: umask: Default Permissions 🎛️
slides.content:
## What New Files Get

`umask` subtracts permission bits from the default (usually 666 for files, 777 for dirs).

- `umask 022` – new files become 644, dirs 755.
- `umask 077` – new files become 600, dirs 700 (maximum privacy).

Set umask in your script if you create sensitive files, or use `chmod` afterwards.

slides.title: Setuid/Setgid Danger ☠️
slides.content:
## Avoid Unless Absolutely Necessary

The setuid bit (`chmod u+s`) makes a script run with the owner's privileges. Bash ignores setuid on scripts for security reasons, but compiled programs can use it. Never rely on setuid shell scripts; use `sudo` instead.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Periodically audit permissions with `find /path -type f -perm /o+w` to find world‑writable files.
